lead: Hialeah plumbing deals with heat, heavy rain, concrete block homes and aging cast-iron drains. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Hialeah.
risk: cast-iron drain failures, slab leaks and storm flooding
risk_short: cast-iron drains, slab leaks and flooding
why: Most Hialeah homes are concrete block on slabs, built from the 1950s to the 1980s. Cast-iron drains under those slabs rot from the inside, and copper supply lines can leak under the floor.
Summer storms and hurricanes flood low streets and back up drains. Many homes have added rooms and converted garages with older plumbing tied in.
utility: Miami-Dade Water and Sewer and the City of Hialeah
water: Hialeah's water comes from the Biscayne Aquifer through Miami-Dade Water and Sewer and the city's own reverse osmosis plant. It is moderately hard.
tips: Have cast-iron drains scoped in older homes.
Shut off the main valve before a hurricane evacuation.
Watch your water bill for slab leak signs.
Get permits for plumbing in room additions.
areas: PipeMend works in Downtown Hialeah, East Hialeah, West Hialeah, Country Club, the Seminola area and every other Hialeah neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Hialeah Building Department, and plumbing contractors are licensed by the Florida Construction Industry Licensing Board.

faq.q: Why do Hialeah homes have drain problems?
faq.a: Many were built with cast-iron drains under the slab. After 40 to 70 years, the iron rusts and cracks, causing slow drains, backups and sewer smells. A camera inspection shows what is needed.
